decisive_diff_evidence: The Get a decryptor for a given room and algorithm API comment and its _getRoomDecryptor implementation are unchanged in both earlier releases. This is not newly introduced ransom wording.

The crypto/index.js source diff only marks sessions for later backup when backup is not yet configured and schedules sending when backupInfo exists. Megolm changes add diagnostics and call this backup queue consistently.
Other source changes implement presence GET, stop TURN retries on 403, add local call-stat collection and DTMF sending, and fix WebRTC negotiation. There are no added or removed package members.

Both browser source maps list the same 128 sources. Only four Matrix sources and four qs sources change; qs implements query-string formatting, parsing and encoding fixes. Dependencies and Babel/TypeScript/minification tooling have ordinary version bumps.

The Browserify re-export of regenerator-runtime is unchanged bundled Babel adapter code. It was paired with devDependencies.olm=https://packages.matrix.org/npm/olm/olm-3.2.1.tgz, also unchanged. It is not the package main ./lib/index.js and does not fetch Olm at require time.
execution_paths: decryptEvent reads event content and room ID, gets a cached or newly instantiated algorithm from DECRYPTION_CLASSES, and delegates to alg.decryptEvent. Megolm decryptEvent validates sender_key/session_id/ciphertext, calls OlmDevice.decryptGroupMessage, and requests missing room keys. There is no victim-file encryption or ransom demand on this path.

backupGroupSession marks crypto-store sessions needing backup. _backupPendingKeys exports those sessions, encrypts their JSON with backupKey, and sends the encrypted session_data through configured baseApis.sendKeyBackup. This is E2EE key backup, not plaintext key theft.

The Browserify module table resolves the bundled regenerator-runtime adapter locally. Package entry points load local SDK modules; declared scripts build, lint, test and publish the SDK, with no consumer install hook.

Decoded fact strings comprise Unicode/URL escapes in qs, punycode and regex handling; a short incidental Base64 decoding yields non-code control bytes. No concealed executable payload was recovered. Browser source is over the 2 MB value-flow budget, so whole-program flow is not assumed; relevant paths were read directly.
